prompt: Extreme close-up from below: a Filipino woman's hand extends a single stem wildflower upward toward an unseen recipient, the arm angled diagonally across the frame. The flower is at the top of the frame; the wrist and forearm recede downward. Persian blue sleeve. The offering gesture fills the composition. Bold diagonal energy.

From directly behind: a small Indigenous girl, about 5, with long dark braided hair, reaches up to offer a handful of wildflowers to a tall white elderly man standing in front of her. He is seen from behind too, bending very slightly to receive them. Just the two figures from behind, the flowers passing between them at waist height.

Strong side profile of a Black teenage girl, looking down at a single flower she holds in both hands at chest level, examining it closely. Her profile faces left. Her hands and the flower are the focal point. The watercolor wash is confident across her face and hair; the pencil sketch defines her features. Vast empty cream to the right.

Low angle looking up: a South Asian man, mid-thirties, holds a small bouquet of prairie wildflowers outward toward the viewer, his arm extended. Seen from below, his face above the bouquet looks warmly at the recipient below. The flowers fill the lower center of frame; his face and the open cream sky above. The gesture is generous and direct.

Overhead top-down view: two hands meeting at center frame. One hand, belonging to a Metis woman, places a single yellow wildflower into the open palm of a white elderly man's hand below. The hands are the entire composition. Seen straight from above. The flower is the only color accent beyond skin and blue sleeve cuffs.

Two profiles facing each other: a Filipino teenage girl on the left and an Indigenous woman in her forties on the right. The girl extends a small bunch of wildflowers across the space between them; the woman's hands receive them. The flowers hang in the space between the two profiles. Pencil sketch defines both faces clearly; wash is bold on the clothing.

Over-the-shoulder from behind a white elderly woman bending slightly to hand a flower to a young child in front of her. The viewer is close behind the woman; her white hair and blue-washed shoulder fill the left side. The child's small reaching hands are visible in front, the flower passing between. The child's face is just barely visible in profile.

Extreme close-up: a young child's two small hands cupping a single flower, offering it forward toward the viewer. The hands fill the lower frame; the flower at center. Just above the hands, the child's chin and lower lip are visible, smiling. Nothing else. The hands and flower are the whole image. Warm amber skin, pencil sketch on the knuckles.

Wide shot from behind: a Black man and a Filipino woman walk side by side along a path through prairie grass, he has just handed her a single wildflower which she holds out slightly, looking at it. Both are small figures in the lower third of the wide frame. Grass in loose upward blue-green strokes flanks the path. Vast warm cream sky above.

A Metis elder woman, seen in three-quarter view from slightly above, bends to place a flower gently into the hair of a small South Asian girl standing in front of her. The elder's weathered hands are delicate and careful. The girl's face is in profile, eyes closed in a pleased expression. The flower is being placed, not yet settled. Tender and precise.

Side profile of an Indigenous teenage boy, facing right, holding a bundle of wildflowers loosely at his side, looking ahead as if about to present them. The flowers hang at hip level, casually held. His profile is sharp pencil line with blue watercolor wash over his jacket. The stems of the flowers are visible as fine pencil marks. Unhurried, natural.

From directly behind: a Filipino woman kneels to be at eye level with a white toddler standing in front of her. The toddler holds up a single wildflower with both chubby hands. The woman's hands are open, ready to receive. Both are seen entirely from behind. The flower is the only thing between them. Simple grass strokes at their feet.
